title: VMC 84 524 sugarcane (NSIC Sc 9): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: VMC 84 524 sugarcane: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: VMC 84 524 sugarcane is a sugarcane variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: VMC 84 524 is a registered sugarcane variety, also sold or known as NSIC Sc 9. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2002 as NSIC 2002 Sc 9. Vict. Expt. Station bred it. It takes about 9.5 months from planting to harvest, with 196 LKg of sugar per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Sc 9, this is the same sugarcane. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [sugarcane variety finder](/crop-varieties/sugarcane), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for sugarcane](/land-preparation/sugarcane-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

VMC 84 524 sugarcane takes about 9.5 months from planting to harvest. That is 1.2 months faster than the average of the 16 sugarcane varieties with a day count, 10.8 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 196 LKg/ha beats the average of its group, 160.71. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Sugar yield is counted in LKg, bags of 50 kilograms of raw sugar per hectare. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Rice field rats](/pests/rice-field-rats).

The pests and diseases that hit sugarcane fields most often: [Rice field rats](/pests/rice-field-rats), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [white grub](/pests/white-grub). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its stalks grew about 241 cm long and 2.84 cm thick. The fiber content is 14 to 15 percent. Trash: semi self trashing, which decides how much cleaning the cane needs before milling.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Matures in 9 to 10 months, can be harvested any month.
**Fruit:** Stalks about 241 cm long, 2.84 cm thick, 1.61 kg, fiber 14 to 15 percent.
About 7 tillers per hill, semi self trashing.
Resistant to downy mildew, leaf scorch, smut, yellow spot and rust.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: early maturing VMC cane with the highest registered sugar yield of the 2002 VMC releases and resistance to all major listed diseases. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant VMC 84 524 sugarcane

Mills pay for sugar, not cane, so compare the sugar yield in LKg per hectare as well as the tonnes of cane. Pick a variety that ratoons well, and one rated against smut and downy mildew, the diseases that cut a ratoon crop short. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation in the Philippines](/land-preparation/land-preparation-philippines).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is NSIC Sc 9 the same as VMC 84 524?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Sc 9 is another name for VMC 84 524, registered as NSIC 2002 Sc 9. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 9.5 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 196 LKg of sugar per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of VMC 84 524?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
